f2llm.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-02: `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-mixed.gguf` supersedes the Q4_K files

The CUDA/CPU audit measured `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-imatrix.gguf` at cosine 0.78 against the F32 file, below the Q4_K acceptance bar of 0.94 (`-q4_k-imatrix-c2` 0.76, plain `-q4_k` 0.59). They remain here unchanged for reproducibility but are **superseded**. The replacement keeps Q4_K+imatrix (134-text calibration corpus) for most matrices, with `ffn_down` at Q6_K, `attn_v` and the last three blocks (25-27) at Q8_0, and token embeddings at Q8_0. On a 78-text panel (13 audit texts plus 65 held-out German/English/code/query texts), minimum cosine against `codefuse-ai/F2LLM-v2-0.6B` (sentence-transformers, FP32) is about 0.96, versus 0.77 for the superseded file. The imatrix used is `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-mixed.imatrix`. Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.

clip.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-02: `clip-text-base-q4_k-mixed.gguf` supersedes `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf`

The CUDA/CPU audit measured `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf` at cosine 0.933 against the F32 file, below the Q4_K bar of 0.94. Part of that gap was a CrispEmbed runtime defect, not the weights: inputs longer than 75 tokens lost their closing EOS on truncation, so pooling read a content token. That is fixed in CrispEmbed (`CRISPEMBED_CLIP_TEXT_KEEP_EOS`, default on). The replacement uses Q4_K+imatrix, with `attn.v` and encoder block 0 at Q8_0 and token embeddings at Q8_0. On a 78-text panel its minimum cosine against `openai/clip-vit-base-patch16` `get_text_features` (CLIPTokenizerFast, FP32) is about 0.988. Older files remain unchanged for reproducibility; `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf` is superseded. Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.
